title: Vault Bridge: Terraform playbook for HSM/KMS integration (draft)
content:
Purpose and scope:

This is a working playbook for integrating a secrets backplane for Redwood Private deployments that bridges customer-managed HSMs (PKCS#11) and cloud KMS providers via HashiCorp Vault. The goal is to provide a Terraform-first set of module notes, upgrade steps, and operational checks for:

- Auto-unseal and key escrow options (HSM vs cloud KMS)
- Secrets engine provisioning and migration paths
- Encryption of Terraform state and CI secrets
- Audit log configuration and retention controls
- Rotation and emergency key-eviction procedures

Assumptions and constraints:

- Customers may run Vault in a VPC or air-gapped on-prem cluster.
- Some customers will bring their own HSMs (PKCS#11/PIV) while others will use cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault).
- We operate a control-plane that must not retain plaintext secrets; integration should minimize operator blast radius.
- Terraform versions: expected compatibility tested on terraform v1.4.x - v1.5.x; providers: vault provider v3.x, cloud provider KMS provider pinned in module.

Non-goals:

- Replacing HashiCorp Vault operational runbooks (this is integration-focused).
- Full FIPS validation guidance (refer to compliance team artifacts).

High-level pattern options (tradeoffs):

1) HSM-backed auto-unseal (on-prem PKCS#11)
   - Pros: keys never leave customer HSM, strong physical security.
   - Cons: complex provisioning, driver/agent lifecycles, firmware compatibility, requires ops access to HSM.

2) Cloud KMS auto-unseal (hybrid)
   - Pros: simpler to bootstrap, managed provider SLAs, easier Terraform integration.
   - Cons: customer may consider it unacceptable for air-gapped scenarios, cross-region latency for unseal calls.

3) Dual-backup: HSM for primary, cloud-KMS wrap for cross-region disaster recovery
   - Pros: best of both worlds; can provide cross-region recovery without exposing HSM master key.
   - Cons: additional complexity and careful access control to prevent key-synchronization abuse.

Recommended architecture (initial default):

- Deploy Vault clusters inside customer VPC with TLS termination at an internal load balancer.
- Use HSM-backed auto-unseal where available; fall back to cloud KMS if HSM not provided.
- Store application secrets in KV v2; use Transit engine for envelope encryption for long-lived artifacts.
- Audit device: syslog -> local collector -> centralized SIEM (with signed audit logs if customer requires).

Terraform module notes (usage pattern and opinionated defaults):

Module: redwood/vault-bridge (internal module)
- Purpose: Provision Vault namespace, mount required engines, configure auto-unseal, bind policies, and create service identities.

Opinionated inputs (important):
- vault_cluster_name (string) – required
- auto_unseal_method (string) – allowed: "hsm", "cloud-kms", "hybrid" (default: "cloud-kms")
- hsm_pkcs11_library_path (string) – optional, only for hsm
- hsm_slot_label (string) – optional
- cloud_provider (string) – one of: aws|gcp|azure (used for provider configuration when auto_unseal_method includes cloud-kms)
- audit_log_destination (string) – syslog|file|splunk|none (default: syslog)
- kv_mounts (list of strings) – e.g., ["apps/", "db/", "ops/"]
- transit_key_names (list) – names for Transit keys to create with rotate/update policies

Outputs:
- vault_addr (string)
- vault_service_account (string / IAM role)

Example (pseudo-terraform snippet):

module "vault_bridge" {
  source                 = "git::https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-modules.git//vault-bridge"
  vault_cluster_name     = "redwood-customer-us-west-2"
  auto_unseal_method     = "hsm"
  hsm_pkcs11_library_path = "/opt/ibm-pkcs11/libpkcs11.so"
  kv_mounts              = ["apps/", "db/"]
  transit_key_names      = ["envelope", "session"]
}

Terraform state considerations:
- Always use remote state (S3/GCS/Azure) with server-side encryption enabled and a customer KMS CMK when possible.
- State files must not contain unsealed Vault master keys or cleartext bootstrap tokens. If bootstrap tokens are created by Terraform, write them to an encrypted temp secret store (Vault agent + wrapped token TTL) and destroy after consumption.
- Enable state locking (dynamoDB for S3 backend) to avoid concurrent apply races with key material.

Upgrade plan (Terraform + providers + HSM firmware):

Pre-upgrade checklist:
- Snapshot HSM configuration and firmware version; retrieve vendor rollback images.
- Export current Vault seal status and a wrapped unseal token (one-time) into an offline, encrypted artifact stored in the customer vault operations safe.
- Run full terraform plan and review provider upgrades in a sandbox cluster.
- Validate CI/CD pipelines can access the KMS for provider operations without exposing credentials to public CI.

Sequential steps (example):
1) Roll out Terraform provider pin updates in a canary workspace with a single Vault node and test auto-unseal.
2) Validate PKCS#11 library path and permissions on nodes; install vendor drivers as part of node bootstrap.
3) If upgrading HSM firmware, coordinate maintenance window with customer and apply via vendor recommended sequence; do NOT upgrade HSM firmware on all HSMs simultaneously (keep a failover HSM).
4) Apply module changes to remaining Vault nodes with gradual rollout, monitoring Audit logs and seal/unseal events.
5) Run post-upgrade smoke tests: create/unwrap wrapped tokens, encrypt/decrypt transit values, rotate a transit key and confirm downstream services can still read envelopes.

Migration plan (cloud-KMS -> HSM):
- Goal: migrate auto-unseal from cloud KMS to on-prem HSM with no downtime.
- Approach: enable HSM auto-unseal in parallel (vault auto-unseal supports multiple unseal backends only by HV options; if not supported, use staged reinit approach):
  1) Stand up HSM and ensure PKCS#11 connectivity.
  2) Configure Vault to use HSM for unseal on a single follower node in staging; test unseal/reseal cycles.
  3) Promote and demote nodes in a rolling fashion while ensuring that at least one node can unseal via cloud KMS during the transition period.
  4) After all nodes successfully use HSM unseal, revoke cloud KMS keys used for unseal and rotate any wrapped tokens.

Secrets handling patterns (best-practices):
- No long-lived plaintext secrets in Git or TF state.
- Use Vault Agent with auto-auth to inject short-lived tokens into pods/VMs.
- Use response-wrapping for any bootstrap secrets emitted by infra provisioning pipelines, TTL <= 5m.
- Transit engine for envelope encryption: application stores encrypted blobs in customer DB; keys remain in Vault. For re-encryption (key rotation), ensure backward-compat script exists to rewrap without data loss.

Audit logging and retention:
- Enable Vault audit logging with a signed backend (file-signed + remote collection) where available.
- Minimum retention for audit logs: 90 days on hot storage, 1 year on cold archive (customer-configurable).
- Ensure audit logs include caller identity, request path, response code, and ACL decision.
- For high-assurance customers: ship logs to customer SIEM over TLS with mutual auth; provide signed timestamps.

Rotation and emergency procedures:
- Transit key rotation: use staged rollouts; support dual-key acceptance window for up to 24h depending on workload.
- HSM key compromise response:
  1) Quarantine affected HSM(s); shift traffic to failover HSM(s).
  2) Rotate Vault root and transit keys immediately; rewrap any wrapped values.
  3) Trigger incident response and forensics; preserve HSM logs and tamper-evidence artifacts.

Testing matrix (recommended automated tests):
- Unit: terraform plan with fixture variables; module-level unit tests (terratest).
- Integration: Vault cluster bootstrapped using module; auto-unseal via HSM + via cloud-KMS; test secret write/read and transit operations.
- Chaos: simulate HSM node loss, KMS throttling, and network partitions to validate failover and unseal behavior.

Rollback plan:
- Keep pre-upgrade artifacts (wrapped unseal token, snapshot of Vault config, Terraform state snapshot) in encrypted ops vault.
- If post-upgrade tests fail, revert Terraform state using remote state snapshot and re-provision nodes to previous AMI/agent version.

Operational run checklist (operator-friendly):
- Verify HSM connectivity: pkcs11-tool -l and vendor agent status.
- Confirm Vault seal status: vault status (TLS, address must be internal LB).
- Check audit stream: last 24h audit entries and signing verification.
- Validate token lifecycle: no service is using long-lived tokens ( > 24h ).

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to support customers with strictly air-gapped environments where even cloud KMS wrapping for DR is disallowed? Need explicit play for manual key transport.
- Confirm supported PKCS#11 libraries across RHEL/CentOS/Ubuntu AMIs in our node images.
- Decide default retention for audit logs per pricing tier.

References and example artifacts:
- Sample terraform module: examples/vault-bridge/README.md (see linked artifacts)
- Vault enterprise doc on HSM: https://www.vaultproject.io/docs/internals/seal#hsm
- Vendor HSM playbooks (IBM/Ayla/Thales internal links – customer-specific)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is an early draft intended to collect operational constraints and Terraform usage patterns. Please annotate with provider-version compatibility, known gotchas for PKCS#11 vendors, and any additional security controls required by compliance.

Checklist before marking final:
- [ ] Add exact provider pins used in CI and PR tests.
- [ ] Add example wrapper script for creating and consuming response-wrapped bootstrap tokens.
- [ ] Insert step-by-step HSM firmware upgrade playbook linked to vendor KB.
- [ ] Add CIR/CD secure variable pattern for ephemeral bootstrap tokens.
